post_text:
More StarHub 5G+ FAQs:
https://www.starhub.com/personal/support/article.html?id=uyu7jnAgiM5NdRhAt0jR79
2. How is StarHub's 5G+ different from 5G?
5G+ builds on regular 5G with added network capacity. You get up to 4x faster speeds, stronger connections in places like indoors, underground, and crowded environments, and a smoother, more consistent experience overall.
9. What are the benefits of 5G+ besides faster speed?
Beyond speed, 5G+ gives you stronger connections in places that are usually tricky for any network, like indoors, underground, and crowded environments. The result is a smoother, more consistent experience overall, not just a faster one.
10. Does 5G+ work while roaming overseas?
Not yet. 5G+ runs on 5G Standalone (SA) technology, and our roaming partners currently only support 5G Non-Standalone (NSA). While roaming, you'll stay connected on 5G NSA or 4G, depending on what's available in that country.
11. How do I get connected to StarHub 5G+?
You'll need three things: a 5G mobile plan, a 5G SIM or eSIM, and a supported 5G+ device
12. How will I know my device is connected to 5G+?
Your network indicator may vary depending on your device manufacturer and software version. For supported Android models, customers will see “5G+” beside network signal strength. E.g. Samsung Galaxy Fold8/Fold8 Ultra/Flip8 will display 5G+.
13. What happens if I'm temporarily unable to connect to the StarHub 5G+ network?
On instances where the 5G+ network is unavailable, you will automatically be switched to our 5G or 4G network to ensure you remain connected online. As soon as 5G+ network becomes accessible, you will automatically be reconnected back.
14. In what frequency band and spectrum(s) is StarHub running its 5G+ network on?
StarHub's 5G Standalone Access (SA) is deployed on 3.5GHz, 2.1GHz and 700MHz spectrum that allows us to enhance and expand our 5G coverage.

thread_title: Double-charged payments by StarHub
post_text:
Does your Starhub account recognise both credits?
Is the amount just paying off a phone (hardware) purchase, or does it include your monthly usage bill too?
If it includes usage, and you can live without the $100 tvis month, I'd be inclined just to leave it, just means youre going to get smaller or no bills for usage in the following months.
If its just paying off a phone only, I'd probably say the same thing, but try to get confirmation they will end the installments 1 month early to make up for it.
If the $100 is really important for you to get back, you cant really do much with GXS, as you willingly made that payment, theres no fraud or error with that payment.
The problem seems to be the DBS payment, it went through so no error from DVS, the problem seems the starhun app just didn't reflect it. You're probably going to rely on Starhubs goodwill to refund.
You could try doing a chargeback for the payment "paid by other means" which covers non-fraud and where the merchant received payment already via a different method/card for the same goods or service. This would only work for the 2nd payment and only for a main scheme card such as Visa or Mastercard where this is a specific chargeback condition covering this situation built into their rules. But honestly its probably not worth it, just consider it as a extra $100 you paid early, so your final payment will also finish a month early.

Signed up to 5G Unlimited+ Max Core. There was no verification of CIS, just needed to provide the promo code.
Roaming in Thailand and Australia was pretty good, with 5G available. Eight did not have 5G roaming in these destinations (only 4G). Outgoing calls and SMS while roaming also works as expected, and from Singapore it's nice to be able to call the foreign number directly without having to jump through v019 hoops.
In Singapore, the plan works as expected with maybe marginally better connectivity compared to eight. IPv6 was available. Overall, the plans are not bad if you are looking for global SMS/calls with some roaming data allowances.
